blogs.title: When 'Angioedema' Isn't Angioedema: The Pitfalls of Neck Swelling in Autoimmune Disease
blogs.description: This post explores the dangerous diagnostic trap of mistaking inflammatory myopathy edema for true angioedema. We analyze why this patient's neck swelling mimicked a deep neck space infection and idiopathic angioedema, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing between histaminergic/bradykinin-mediated pathways and muscle-derived inflammation. Key takeaways include recognizing 'pseudo-angioedema' as a red flag for underlying myositis and avoiding unnecessary epinephrine or C1-inhibitor therapies.

blogs.title: CK > 16,000: Why Creatine Kinase is Your Best Friend in Unexplained Edema
blogs.description: Focusing on the pivotal role of laboratory diagnostics, this article dissects the decision-making process that led to checking CK in a patient with neck swelling. We discuss the clinical threshold for ordering myositis panels in 'atypical' presentations where standard infectious workups are negative. The post highlights how a massively elevated CK (16,184 U/L) immediately pivoted the differential away from ENT pathology toward systemic autoimmune disease, serving as a masterclass in efficient triage.

blogs.title: The Anti-SAE1 Signature: Recognizing the Silent Killer in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: A deep dive into serology, specifically focusing on Anti-Small Ubiquitin-Like Modifier Activating Enzyme 1 (SAE1) antibodies. Unlike classic DM presentations dominated by Mi-2 or Jo-1 antibodies, SAE1-positive dermatomyositis presents unique challenges regarding malignancy risk and pulmonary involvement. This post reviews current literature on SAE1 profiles, their association with dysphagia and ILD, and why identifying this specific antibody subtype matters for long-term surveillance strategies.

blogs.title: Don't Miss the Perifascicular Clue: Biopsy Findings That Seal the Diagnosis
blogs.description: An educational piece centered on pathophysiology and histopathology. While clinical signs like Gottron's papules were absent in this case, the muscle biopsy provided definitive proof via perifascicular atrophy and C5b-9 deposition. This post explains *why* these specific microscopic features distinguish dermatomyositis from polymyositis or necrotizing myopathy, reinforcing that even without classic rashes ('amyopathic' or 'hypomyopathic' variants), histologic confirmation remains gold standard.

blogs.title: Airway Safety First: Managing Dysphagia and Respiratory Compromise in Acute Myositis
blogs.description: Addressing the immediate life-threats presented by this case: aspiration pneumonitis and airway compromise due to pharyngeal muscle inflammation. This post discusses the urgency of securing the airway in patients with rapid-onset neck swelling and dysphagia, even when oxygen saturation appears normal initially. It covers multidisciplinary management involving speech therapy (video fluoroscopic swallow studies), nutritional support (NG tubes), and aggressive immunomodulation to prevent permanent respiratory failure.
